lush.note: Several oscillators a voice, detuned 5 to 20 cents apart (a pitch node each, semitones ±0.05 to ±0.2 on voice.frequency), maybe an octave or a fifth below quietly; then chorus. Scale the level down as oscillators are added: they sum.
lush.check: stereoCorrelation falls (under about 0.6 with chorus); the picture's harmonics shimmer and thicken.

bright.note: Harmonic-rich sources (saw, narrow pulse, a wavetable's later cycles) with the filter well open; for vibrant, keep it moving: a slow lfo or beatlfo on cutoff, or a filter envelope on each note.
bright.check: centroidHz above about 1500 for a lead or keys; the 2k to 8k bands within 10 dB of the 500 band.

dark.note: A low-pass with cutoff around 300 to 1500 Hz and little resonance, cutoff key-tracked (a scaled voice.frequency in its list) so high notes don't vanish; sine, triangle or a sub rather than bright sources.
dark.check: centroidHz under about 800; the 4k and 8k bands 20 dB or more below the 250 to 500 bands.

warm.note: A ladder low-pass around 1 to 3 kHz with a little resonance, a touch of shaper drive (2 to 4), and slow drift: voice.seed into a pitch node, a few cents.
warm.check: centroidHz around 600 to 1500; the 250 to 1k bands lead, with the 4k band 10 to 20 dB under them.

eerie.note: Unsteady pitch (a slow lfo, 0.1 to 0.5 Hz, into a pitch node by ±10 to 30 cents, plus voice.seed drift), a quiet layer at an odd interval (a tritone, +6, or a major seventh, +11), a dark filter, slow attack, and a long reverb (decay 4 to 8 s). Some pinknoise through a band-pass for air.
eerie.check: The picture's harmonic lines waver, and a tail rings on after the notes; centroidHz low to mid.

glassy.note: Sine or triangle partials, some inharmonic (ratios like 2.76 or 3.5), each with its own fast decay; or the harmonics wavetable; a high-pass to clear the lows, and a bright reverb (damping high).
glassy.check: Clean, separate lines in the picture that fade top first; centroidHz high, little between the lines.

gritty.note: Shaper drive 10 to 40, or a waveshaper (hardClip for edge), before the filter so it can tame the fizz; bitcrush (bits 6 to 10, downsample 2 to 6) for lo-fi crunch. Drive adds level, so bring the output down.
gritty.check: The 4k to 16k bands rise and the picture fills in between harmonics; a note still peaks near -10 dBFS.

airy.note: Pinknoise or noise through an svf band-pass or high-pass, on the note's envelope, mixed well under the tone.
airy.check: The 8k and 16k bands rise; a haze above the harmonics in the picture while notes sound.

wide.note: Chorus; each voice panned a little by voice.seed (a pan node in the voice, voice: [left, right]); different delay or reverb settings on each side. Keep bass mono.
wide.check: stereoCorrelation between about 0.2 and 0.6 (below 0 means phase trouble, and it vanishes in mono).

punchy.note: An amp envelope with attack under 5 ms, decay 0.1 to 0.4 s and low sustain; a filter envelope opening on the attack and closing fast (an adsr into a pitch node's semitones on cutoff).
punchy.check: Each onset in the picture is bright and tall, then narrows within a few hundred ms.

soft.note: Attack 0.2 to 1 s, release 1 to 3 s, a low-pass and slow movement (wavetable position or cutoff on a slow lfo); for evolving, two lfos at unrelated rates.
soft.check: No sharp onsets in the picture: notes fade in, and the bands drift slowly over time.

supersaw.note: Five to seven saws a voice, detuned symmetrically up to ±0.3 semitones, the outer ones quieter, panned apart; a gentle low-pass, chorus and reverb.
supersaw.check: stereoCorrelation well under 0.5; dense beating harmonics in the picture; a bright centroid.

strings.note: A pulse whose width an lfo moves (0.5 ± 0.2 at 0.3 to 1 Hz), a second detuned, attack 0.3 to 0.8 s, a low-pass around 3 to 5 kHz, chorus.
strings.check: Slow attacks and a gently moving comb of harmonics in the picture; a mid centroid.

bell.note: A sine carrier whose frequency input is [voice.frequency, modulator]: a sine modulator at a ratio (3.5 for a bell, 1 for an e-piano, via a pitch node) multiplied (mul) by voice.frequency, a fast-decaying adsr, and the index (scale 1 to 5). The index envelope makes the strike bright and the tail pure.
bell.check: Many lines at the onset collapsing to a few as it rings; inharmonic lines for a bell.

acid.note: A saw or square into a ladder with resonance 0.7 to 0.9; a short decay envelope (0.1 to 0.3 s) on cutoff by 2 to 4 octaves, deeper with velocity for accents. No glide yet.
acid.check: A resonant peak sweeping down from each onset in the picture.

sub.note: A sine (or a triangle for more presence) at the note, a short attack, mono, maybe a little shaper drive.

pluck.note: A plucked string: a burst of noise into a delay tuned by period, fed back through onepole damping, its gain from loopgain; or a bright saw with a fast filter envelope.
pluck.check: Bright onsets darkening as they decay; the tail falls away rather than holding.
